versions.body:
<!-- qwen-release-notes:v1 -->

## Highlights

_See the complete change list below._

## Breaking Changes

No known breaking changes.

## Complete Change List

### Features

- feat(web-shell): explain background tasks from the composer chips ([#17398](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17398)) by @wenshao
- Adds the backend-neutral unified chat surface contract and capability guards for Web Shell, with no user-visible behavior change yet. ([#17520](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17520)) by @wenshao
- feat(channels): add GitHub as the third managed channel adapter ([#17511](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17511)) by @wenshao
- Lets Generated UI cards preserve view state across page reloads, reopened conversations, and forks. ([#17522](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17522)) by @qqqys
- feat(web-shell): send to another session with /send ([#17539](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17539)) by @qqqys
- Removes daemon dependencies from shared approval and composer components so the managed chat kernel can use them without loading daemon code. ([#17661](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17661)) by @wenshao
- Adds a send-only Generic Webhook Channel that posts notification, prompt, and scheduled-task results as JSON to a configured HTTPS endpoint, with optional Bearer authentication. ([#17610](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17610)) by @jkxiao
- Managed agents now notify owners when attachments are retired and classify suspension age-out waits with control-plane wait codes. ([#17681](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17681)) by @doudouOUC
- Adds Generic Webhook destinations in the Web Shell Channel editor, with endpoint URL, optional Bearer token, and local/private receiver options. ([#17405](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17405)) by @jkxiao
- Session switching now shows the artifact count immediately from session metadata, before full loading completes. ([#17518](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17518)) by @wenshao
- Enables Mods in ACP sessions for qwen --acp, Zed, and the VS Code companion when experimental.mods is enabled. ([#17693](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17693)) by @qqqys
- Applies the --max-sse-connections admission budget to all daemon stream surfaces, with shared occupancy accounting and logged refusal when the limit is exceeded. ([#17662](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17662)) by @wenshao
- Adds an experimental WeCom managed-channel adapter that routes private-chat messages into bound Managed Agent Sessions and returns replies over the authenticated WebSocket. ([#17441](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17441)) by @wenshao
- Installs and pins default Workspace Skills from an optional catalog when a Workspace Session is created without caller-provided Skills or an explicit pin list. ([#17703](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17703)) by @doudouOUC
- Adds a status-tinted Goal marker to Web Shell sidebar session rows so sessions with active Goals are recognizable and can be opened from the marker. ([#17515](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17515)) by @wenshao
- Adds a Traditional Chinese UI locale to Web Shell and VS Code companion chrome, with zh-TW, zh-HK, zh-MO, and zh-Hant resolving to 繁體中文 [zh-TW]. ([#17421](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17421)) by @callmeYe
- Marks shortened inbound messages from WeCom, DingTalk, and GitHub managed adapters with a truncation notice while keeping them within character and byte limits. ([#17726](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17726)) by @wenshao
- Hosted Harness now suspends idle managed-agent sessions after active work drains and cold-opens them on the next request. ([#17690](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17690)) by @doudouOUC
- Adds an opt-in setting that skips models exhausted by capacity errors for the rest of the turn and re-probes them on the next turn. ([#17377](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17377)) by @wenshao
- Binds DingTalk persisted ledger to registration identity so pending messages are not replayed under a different registration of the same robot app. ([#17742](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17742)) by @wenshao
- Adds an inject channel dispatchMode that delivers incoming messages to the running turn so the agent can read them at the next tool-batch boundary. ([#15634](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15634)) by @Eric-GoodBoy-Tech
- Adds a workspace artifact library to the Managed Agent Web UI for browsing, previewing, and downloading artifacts across sessions. ([#17728](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17728)) by @wenshao
- Adds opt-in native screen-reader presentation for the CLI with keyboard navigation, stable completed-reply announcements, and semantic history while Ink remains default. ([#17500](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17500)) by @chiga0
- Moves the Artifacts (N) header entry to the right panel so clicking it toggles a dedicated session-scoped Artifacts list tab. ([#17689](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17689)) by @wenshao
- Adds the daemon chat intent lifecycle core so submit, cancel, approval, and question states are settled from authoritative evidence rather than transport responses alone. ([#17709](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17709)) by @wenshao
- Wakes the Managed Session bound to a watched pull request with private prompts when CI fails, conflicts appear, or the head changes, without posting publicly. ([#17665](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17665)) by @wenshao
- Adds an opt-in setting, qwen.managed-agent.runtime-broker.mcp-parking.enabled, to keep idle MCP connections across suspension so reopened sessions reuse them. ([#17749](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17749)) by @doudouOUC
- Shows a workflow's declared meta.phases as Not started lanes before they begin, then replaces each lane when the script reaches that phase. ([#17782](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17782)) by @qqqys
- Adds managed-agent support for external Shell workers to publish control-plane events. ([#17478](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17478)) by @yiliang114
- Adds an off-by-default QQ bot option exposing tools for agents to send local files, images, videos, and voice messages. ([#15450](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15450)) by @Eric-GoodBoy-Tech
- Adds a Microsoft Teams channel extension with personal chats, group mentions, thread isolation, and createTeamsIngress host webhook setup. ([#15620](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15620)) by @XIQIXIQIXIQI
- feat(telemetry): record OpenRouter routing backend and generation id ([#16495](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16495)) by @2SinceJuly
- WebShell transcripts expose an optional overscan prop so hosts can tune or disable the offscreen row buffer for virtualized message lists. ([#17807](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17807)) by @callmeYe
- DingTalk managed-agent replies now render as a single editable native card that updates as more reply segments arrive, instead of plain text messages. ([#17748](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17748)) by @wenshao
- feat(core): name the output budget when truncation rejects a write ([#16632](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16632)) by @xxwtiancai
- feat(web-shell): let hosts disable the composer glow ([#17814](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17814)) by @callmeYe
- feat(core): run ACP sessions on the shared agent loop by default ([#17744](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17744)) by @qqqys
- feat(cli): run background workflows in headless mode ([#17809](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17809)) by @qqqys
- Shows Mod-rewritten assistant reply rows in the Web Shell while preserving original text for history, copy, search, and branching. ([#17718](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17718)) by @qqqys
- Adds a --timeout option to /model --vision for setting visionBridgeTimeoutMs, accepting seconds or ms-style values and applying immediately. ([#17830](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17830)) by @qqqys
- Adds the daemon chat controller so incoming daemon events are bound to the correct attempt before settling, preventing late events from affecting finished chat attempts. ([#17794](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17794)) by @wenshao
- Binds the managed GitHub adapter ledger to its registration identity so pending comments are not replayed under a different registration. ([#17775](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17775)) by @wenshao
- feat(managed-agent): clarify Web UI parity and wire local terminal ([#17795](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17795)) by @wenshao
- feat(managed-agent): stamp clean suspensions for wake dispatch ([#17908](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17908)) by @doudouOUC
- feat(core): run OpenTUI on the shared agent loop by default ([#17745](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17745)) by @qqqys
- feat(acp): end a tool-calling turn when queued input is sent now ([#17825](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17825)) by @qqqys
- feat(serve): add daemon restart recovery inbox ([#17677](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17677)) by @wenshao
- feat(web-shell): worktree carry metadata + snapshot-then-delete cleanup (#17237, P6 partial) ([#17533](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17533)) by @wenshao
- feat(acp): deliver pending async hook output on the default legacy round ([#17890](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17890)) by @wenshao
- feat(web-shell): bind the daemon chat controller to the session provider ([#17895](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17895)) by @wenshao
- feat(managed-agent): degrade process components per package in content-only extension runtimes ([#17944](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17944)) by @doudouOUC
- feat(channels): bind the email ledger to its registration identity ([#17925](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17925)) by @wenshao

### Bug Fixes

- fix(verify-pr): harden the watch-state shape guard, container nonce, and VM prose ([#17440](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17440)) by @wenshao
- fix(external-context): deflake cumulative-deadline deletion timing ([#17342](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17342)) by @qwen-code-dev-bot
- fix(serve): reserve listener headroom from SSE and reap stalled writers by default ([#17502](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17502)) by @wenshao
- fix(triage): fail closed when QWEN_TRIAGE_DRAFT_DIR is unset in CI ([#17549](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17549)) by @yiliang114
- fix(managed-agent): recover vanished Harness admissions safely ([#17521](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17521)) by @doudouOUC
- Fixes Web Shell so PR watch deep links can be served before authentication, improving direct link access. ([#17119](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17119)) by @Afloat16
- Updates the Read unchanged-file message to tell users to re-read with a different offset or limit when earlier content is unavailable or out-of-band changes are suspected. ([#17465](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17465)) by @callmeYe
- On touch devices and narrow viewports, the composer model picker now opens as a bottom sheet with model search and reasoning controls, while desktop behavior stays unchanged. ([#17401](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17401)) by @callmeYe
- Limits Grep fallback searches to tracked and non-ignored untracked files so results match git-grep and avoid excluded build output. ([#17530](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17530)) by @callmeYe
- Recovers resubmitted managed-agent turns that are already accepted and, when the parked execution is ready, drives its continuation instead of leaving it stalled. ([#17680](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17680)) by @doudouOUC
- Managed Web Shell now shows request, session, and recovery errors as normal conversation messages, with retry via message link or Ctrl+Y and fewer separate recovery panels. ([#17557](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17557)) by @yiliang114
- Keeps managed DingTalk replies sent in multiple chunks from being truncated and documents why no aggregate send limit is applied. ([#17529](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17529)) by @wenshao
- Cold worktree restoration now delays automatic work until ownership validation and working-directory restore finish, preventing blocked restores and preserving pending questions. ([#17654](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17654)) by @doudouOUC
- Web Shell now removes the extra gap under /send records and keeps each reply visible beside its Cross-session message card when turns are collapsed. ([#17686](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17686)) by @qqqys
- /verify-pr --watch now registers its watch round before prepare, and --start no longer requires --artifact-dir, improving liveness without breaking existing callers. ([#17550](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17550)) by @wenshao
- Long-running processes now release idle JSONL append locks after successful or failed writes settle, reducing lock accumulation. ([#17577](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17577)) by @Afloat16
- Web Shell Memory panel now has a Refresh control that reloads the file list and retries the selected file without closing the panel, restoring editing when reads succeed. ([#17108](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17108)) by @Afloat16
- SDK header merging now treats HTTP header names case-insensitively, so caller headers override transport defaults instead of creating duplicate values. ([#17579](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17579)) by @Afloat16
- CLI exit cleanup now preserves pending cleanup work when handlers unregister, preventing skipped or repeated cleanup during shutdown. ([#17572](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17572)) by @Afloat16
- Stops delivering buffered SSE events after a stream is cancelled, preventing stale session updates. ([#17569](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17569)) by @Afloat16
- Cancels heartbeats for sessions removed or replaced during heartbeat registration, preventing leaked timers. ([#17117](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17117)) by @Afloat16
- Custom commands now preserve argument text literally during prompt expansion, so $$ and $& are not reinterpreted. ([#17367](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17367)) by @Afloat16
- Keeps Python SDK initialization running when one waiting control call is cancelled, allowing other calls and prompt input to continue. ([#17499](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17499)) by @Afloat16
- Shows an amber busy marker in Web Shell sidebar session rows when background work is running and aligns row actions with that state. ([#17676](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17676)) by @wenshao
- Delivers completed background async hook output to the model on the next turn instead of silently dropping it. ([#17477](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17477)) by @wenshao
- Labels shell tool results as Output (stdout and stderr combined) and Execution Error, while keeping compatibility with earlier labels. ([#17685](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17685)) by @qqqys
- CLI and Web Shell copy extraction now keeps fence-like lines inside copied code and does not extract math from code blocks, reducing truncated copies. ([#17578](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17578)) by @Afloat16
- ACP Java SDK now returns selected file lines joined by normal newlines instead of path separators, preventing corrupted file content shown to the agent. ([#17688](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17688)) by @Afloat16
- The SDK now clears permission callback deadlines after failures, preventing stray timeout rejections, crashes, or leftover timers after a denial. ([#17581](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17581)) by @Afloat16
- Web Shell change overview now limits its commit fallback to the current session's own commits and hides it when no reliable session start exists. ([#17514](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17514)) by @wenshao
- Raises the document export renderer JavaScript size budget so newly added Web Shell transcript copy does not fail the build. ([#17746](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17746)) by @wenshao
- SDK now rejects oversized peer frames before dispatch, even when completed in one chunk, and stops overflowing batches while preserving valid separate frames. ([#17576](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17576)) by @Afloat16
- Managed DingTalk streams now centralize reconnection so a single drop starts at most one reconnect chain, and concurrent connect calls join the in-progress attempt. ([#17691](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17691)) by @wenshao
- Cancelling a composer image batch now stops queued image reads that have not started, preventing unnecessary reads and base64 allocation after cancellation. ([#17705](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17705)) by @cactuser-Lu
- Restores managed-agent class-size and facade-population gate checks without changing runtime behavior, fixing deterministic gate failures left on main. ([#17753](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17753)) by @doudouOUC
- SDK now waits for actual child termination, classifies intentional shutdown, preserves failures, and tears down transport before rejecting pending Query and MCP requests. ([#17580](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17580)) by @Afloat16
- Fixes QQ bot direct chats so voice attachments from qqbot.ugcimg.cn are downloaded and delivered as audio instead of empty turns. ([#15339](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15339)) by @mvanhorn
- Shows the managed composer attachment entry for unbound active Sessions when their Harness supports input attachments. ([#17722](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17722)) by @wenshao
- Stabilizes the composer toolbar near width thresholds so approval and model labels no longer shift or disappear when the chat-width toggle appears. ([#17729](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17729)) by @callmeYe
- Fixes qwen-managed-agent-server tool-result publication failures when embedded with json-schema-validator 2.x. ([#17752](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17752)) by @yiliang114
- The delete dialog now blocks deleting any session with running background work and shows the reason, while the current session remains deletable once no work is running. ([#17713](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17713)) by @wenshao
- Time to first token for streamed requests now starts when the request is dispatched, making TTFT and related timing metrics more accurate. ([#17790](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17790)) by @qqqys
- Sessions that contain only side records now show their artifact count on first open, and remaining artifact-summary display issues are fixed. ([#17711](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17711)) by @wenshao
- fix(web-shell): Group approval scopes in a dropdown ([#17801](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17801)) by @callmeYe
- fix(ci): raise the CodeQL JavaScript cap to 180m after the nightly overran 90m ([#17808](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17808)) by @yiliang114
- fix(serve): pin remote-access admission and non-REST shutdown drain (#17712) ([#17737](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17737)) by @wenshao
- Completes Russian UI coverage in Desktop and CLI and keeps long account-menu labels on one line. ([#17719](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17719)) by @callmeYe
- Fixes permission rules so Windows drive-letter and UNC absolute paths match correctly, including Always Allow entries. ([#17810](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17810)) by @yiliang114
- Allows LocalDirectory writes of valid text beginning with a UTF-8 BOM while still rejecting invalid unpaired surrogates. ([#17820](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17820)) by @yiliang114
- fix(web-shell): evict aborted mention cache lookups ([#17826](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17826)) by @yiliang114
- Ensures JSONL logs remain readable after an interrupted append by adding a leading newline before the next record when the previous record is unterminated. ([#17771](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17771)) by @wenshao
- Adds missing Russian translations for experimental.mods, visionBridgeTimeoutMs, and /model --vision --timeout CLI messages. ([#17858](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17858)) by @wenshao
- Compression now reduces or refuses summarization requests that cannot fit the model window and recovers once from context-length rejections. ([#15936](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15936)) by @yanyukang2003-ux
- Web Shell markdown images that point to local paths or fail to load now render as selectable text chips instead of broken placeholders. ([#17866](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17866)) by @doudouOUC

## Desktop

### Improvements
- OpenCode 1 now offers the upgrade to OpenCode 2.0. OpenCode 2 downloads in the background and installs only when you choose: Restart to upgrade, Upgrade on quit, or Later. Your sessions, projects, and settings are kept. Plugins made for OpenCode 1 need an update.

## Core

### Bugfixes
- Sessions with many images no longer send oversized requests. When the images in a session's history pass 25 MiB, the oldest are replaced with a placeholder.
- A provider error for a request body that is too large now starts compaction and a retry instead of failing the turn.

## Core

### Bugfixes
- OpenCode 1 now stays on the 1.x release line: update checks use only the npm `opencode-ai` latest version, so 1.x installs are never offered a 2.x build as a regular update.
- Upgrading to OpenCode 2 remains a separate, explicit choice through the 2.0 offer in `/update` or `opencode upgrade --major`.
- Fix upgrades for installs managed by yarn.
- Skip 1.x updates for Homebrew Core installs, which now track OpenCode 2, and check tap and Chocolatey availability before offering an update.
- The install script refuses to install 2.x versions.

versions.name: v5.1.81
versions.body:
### Changed

- The `programming` skill's language gate now routes rendered web work (`.html`, `.css`, `.jsx`, `.tsx`, `.vue`, `.svelte`, `.astro`, or any task that ships a UI) to the `frontend` skill before the first line of UI code. It tells the agent to take the look from the frontend skill's references when there is no design direction (no named brand, reference, `DESIGN.md`, or existing styled UI to match), and to finish only after `visual-qa` passes on the rendered surface. ([#14604](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14604), fixes [#14602](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/14602))

### Fixed

- Memory sync: a sign-out now retires the trust pin of the account it signs out of, so `omo account show --account <id>` no longer answers `joined` once that sign-in's keys are gone. Plain `omo account forget` (the desktop's sign-out of a CLI-item session) used to retire nothing. It now reads the stored sign-in first to find its account. A stored sign-in that cannot be read is still deleted and its pin is left; one warning line is printed only after the delete succeeds. A forget that fails on a locked store reports only that error (#12308, #12384). ([#13642](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13642)) ([#14533](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14533))
- Memory sync: some sign-ins earned their pin before `omo sync` recorded their account. On a refused refresh, plain `forget`, `forget --device` and `adopt --replace`, omo now asks the service for that account, as `omo logout` already did, and retires the pin when the service names it. It asks only while a live pin exists and the access token has not expired; on a refused refresh, the token may still be valid in the 30 s before expiry, when the refresh runs. An expired token is never sent. A pin whose account stays unknown is kept, and omo prints one line naming `omo account retire-sync --account <id>` to clear it, because `omo account show` keeps answering `joined` for it (#12383, #13662). ([#13642](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13642)) ([#14533](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14533))

### Added

- `omo sync status` (and `--json`) shows this device's memory sync state: the signed-in account, whether this device has joined and whether its sync switch is on, the account's devices with their sync membership and last-seen time, pending join requests, and whether an engine is running on this machine. It writes no sync state, prints no key material, and each section reports its own failure instead of failing the command. ([#14437](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14437), fixes [#14435](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/14435)) ([#14533](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14533))

versions.body:
### Fixed

- The `/remote` close in the TUI follows `thread_close`'s close contract (#14234). A close refused because the thread has messages it has not read names `/remote close <session> --force` and lists those messages, or says the ids are unavailable on that device's engine. The picker then offers "Close anyway". A forced close lists the messages it dropped. The refusal's `details.reason` is the engine's own reason (`turn_active` or `work_pending`). ([#14246](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14246), fixes [#14245](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/14245)) ([#14248](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14248))
- Thread tools: a command for a thread whose session parked on another device after it was listed no longer fails `unsupported` with advice to update omo on that device. The device service answers such a command `route_unlisted` (its host no longer lists that session, so nothing was sent to it). `thread_close` now answers `closed: false, reason: "not_live"`, and the other thread tools answer `not_resumable`, as for a session that ended there. A create, or a reopen's session-file lookup, refused that way is `host_unavailable`, with a retry. ([#14237](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14237), fixes [#14233](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/14233)) ([#14248](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14248))
- The cold-wake session host unit (and every other unit or plist the cold-wake install writes) is now written 0644 under any umask. Under umask 077 it was written 0600, because a file's creation mode is masked by the umask; the mode is now set explicitly before the file is moved into place. ([#14249](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14249), fixes [#14247](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/14247)) ([#14248](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14248))
- A cold-wake unit or plist an earlier build already left 0600 is set back to 0644 the next time the install (or a refresh to a newer runtime) finds its content unchanged, with no reload or restart. A file this user cannot change the mode of (another owner's, or on a read-only filesystem) is left as it is and the install still succeeds. ([#14249](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14249)) ([#14248](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14248))

### Changed

- **`thread_close` no longer drops messages a thread has not read unless you ask it to.** Before, it always interrupted the session and silently dropped any messages queued behind its run. Now:
  - A busy thread with unread messages is refused `turn_active`. The refusal names those messages (`pending_deliveries`) and gives the `force` option.
  - `thread_close({ thread, force: true })` closes it anyway.
  - Every close result carries `dropped_deliveries`, the messages it handed back unread (an empty list when there were none).
  - An idle thread still closes without `force`, even when an interrupted run left messages stranded (#14169); those are listed too.
  - On a device whose engine cannot name its queued messages (older than code-yeongyu/senpi#7006), a default close never interrupts. It says the message ids are unavailable there, and `force: true` still closes it.
  - `omo remote close` takes `--force` and reports the dropped messages as well. versions.body:
**A thread send now reaches a session that is not running, on this device or on another of your devices, and starts it.** It needs senpi 2026.11.15-2 or later (omo pins it), and device service 0.1.31 or later on both devices for a wake from another device. A reply to a sender on another device reads only that device's sessions instead of the whole account listing; a send to a live session that is paused or holds a Stop answers `queued` with `waiting_on: { kind: "hold", device }`; and `waiting_on.kind` in a `thread_send` result can be `approval`, `hold` or `wake`. ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))

### Changed

- `omo remote enable` now sets the device up in one command after `omo login`. It installs the OmO device service when none runs, registers this omo's agent dir with it, turns remote sessions on, and installs and starts the always-on session host unit. If you signed in before the device service was installed, it also links that sign-in to the service, so `omo login` then `omo remote enable` leaves the device connected. Running it again changes nothing that is already in place (#13594). ([#13602](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13602)) ([#13606](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13606))
- `omo remote status` also shows this device's own units as the service manager reports them: the session host unit (running, enabled, pinned host), the device service's unit, whether the cold-wake entry is in place, and the agent dir omo registers. With `--json` these are a `local` object beside the status fields (#13594). ([#13602](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13602)) ([#13606](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13606))
- Thread gateway: waking a session that is not running is on (#13037). It runs on senpi 2026.11.15-2 or later (omo now pins it), the release whose session release drops a woken session's retained record. A message from another of your devices wakes a session here once both devices run device service 0.1.31 or later. The local omo daemon (`omo daemon run`, or the device service's cold-wake unit) registers this device's agent dir with the device service and takes deliveries as soon as it starts, with no session open. ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: the operator daemon declares the delivery consumer as soon as it loads omo, with no session open (#13037 cold wake). `omo daemon run` sends the daemon it ensured senpi's `warm`, so a daemon the device service starts on demand can be handed deliveries before any session runs. A warm that is refused or unsupported prints one line and the run still exits 0. ([#13596](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13596)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: the session wake loads from its own sidecar (`extensions/omo-wake.js` behind `#omo-wake-runtime`): the carrier, the delivery consumer and the device-service client never enter the main `omo.js` bundle, which carries only lazy shells; the ensured host's idle-exit setting is read inside the sidecar. ([#13456](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13456)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: waking a session that is not running needs no setting (#13037). A `thread_send` from this machine to a session here that is not running now starts it by default, and the answer is `queued` with `waiting_on: { kind: "wake" }`. `session_wake.same_device` stays in the configuration schema only as an explicit opt-out (`false`), read for the target session's own project. The wake starts on senpi 2026.11.15-2 or later (senpi#6449), which omo now pins. ([#13456](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13456)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: when no operator host is running, a session that is not running still starts (#13037). Before it opens the session, the carrier asks the engine's own `host ensure --policy never`, from omo's daemon launch spec, on the socket `thread_create` uses. A running host is reused whatever its build; one is started only when nothing answers. The ensured host runs with `omo daemon`'s own host environment: the agent directory is named (`OMO_AGENT_DIR`) and the configured `task.host_idle_exit_ms` rides along (`SENPI_RPC_HOST_IDLE_EXIT_MS`) instead of the launch spec's default, and from a source tree the launch spec resolves to the plugin's tracked copy so the CLI is always handed a file that exists. ([#13456](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13456)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: a delivery from another device is no longer gated on the device service's wake switch being told on. While this engine's delivery consumer is served (from its serving acknowledgement, before its startup pending sweep, so a remote row that sweep wakes is never told the gate is off), the carrier opens the session. The consumer serves on senpi 2026.11.15-2 or later with device service 0.1.31 or later, and it no longer reads the wake the service tells: the wake switch it tracked (`wakeAllowed`, the `delivery.wake` event) had no production reader left. ([#13456](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13456)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- The delivery consumer (design 5.4) runs beside the carrier. The engine minimum for a woken session, `MIN_WAKE_ENGINE_VERSION` (A8.1, senpi 2026.11.15-2, the release that drops a released session's retained record), gates the carrier as well. A device service older than 0.1.31 does not carry the delivery protocol, so on it the consumer serves nothing and does not ask again. ([#13455](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13455)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- The gateway store's schema moves to version 12: three nullable columns on deliveries and a unique index on the new ledger id. The first process on this release migrates the store; any process still on the previous build then reports the store's "schema too new" error on its thread tools and inbox drain until it restarts. ([#13208](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13208)) ([#13279](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13279)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: once a build carrying this store ships, every gateway store open runs the schema step to version 13 (one new table, `woken_sessions`) and raises the store's `user_version` for good. An older build, or a rolled-back one, that shares the same agent directory then refuses to open that store with its "schema too new" error until it is upgraded again. ([#13212](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13212)) ([#13279](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13279)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- A reply to a message that came from another of your devices goes to the session on that device that sent it, whether you reply by its session id or by the name it gave. A session on another device, or on this one, that only carries the same id or name no longer receives the reply. ([#13218](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13218), part of [#13037](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/13037)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))

### Fixed

- An omo engine on a device whose device service runs on a non-default `--state-dir` now registers with it: `deviceServiceStateDir` takes a non-empty absolute `OMO_DEVICE_SERVICE_STATE_DIR`, then the `device-service.location.json` discovery file beside the default dir, and only then `~/.omo/device-service` (#13597). ([#13598](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13598)) ([#13606](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13606))
- A remote worktree remove refused for an empty reflog now says reflogs may be off in the repository, instead of claiming they are: an expired or deleted reflog looks the same (#13542 follow-up). ([#13546](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13546)) ([#13606](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13606))
- Thread gateway: the session wake keeps working after the session that started it ends (#13037). The carrier and the delivery consumer are one per agent directory for the whole process, but they used the first session's gateway store, which that session's shutdown closed, so every later wake in the process failed. The running wake now opens its own store for the life of the process. ([#13596](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13596)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: the carrier re-checks the sender's peer admission at the moment of every open of a row from another device (#13456 review follow-up), so the retry and lease-takeover paths - which the accept-time check of the consumer and the before-turn check of the drain bracketed but nothing else covered - start nothing when the answer is refused or unknown. A lease takeover now consults the same allowance a wake does, ending its record when nothing queued allows the open; the runtime answers the carrier's admission ask on the live delivery port, so the startup pending sweep's own wakes are admitted too. ([#13511](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13511)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: the session wake loads from its own sidecar (`extensions/omo-wake.js` behind `#omo-wake-runtime`): the carrier, the delivery consumer and the device-service client never enter the main `omo.js` bundle, which carries only lazy shells. ([#13457](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13457)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: a consumer failure that changes kind (a device that answers nothing and then refuses the declaration) is warned again: the retry loop's one-warning rule is keyed on the failure itself, not on merely being down, and still stays silent while the same failure repeats. ([#13457](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13457)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: the delivery consumer listens before it declares itself, so the records the device service hands it right after the acknowledgement are no longer dropped. It counts as serving from that acknowledgement, so a session it wakes during its own start is opened, not left switched off. ([#13457](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13457)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: the delivery consumer is started again after it dies (#13457 review): a device service that answers nothing, refuses the declaration, or restarts under a served connection no longer leaves remote wake off for the engine's life. A failed start closes its port and reports itself, a connection that ends during the startup sweep leaves no stale serving consumer behind, and a connect failure the client reports is logged instead of dropped. ([#13457](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13457)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: the wake switch the service tells (`delivery.wake`) has no reader since the carrier's gate moved to the consumer serving, so the consumer no longer tracks it. The conformance fakes the production-port test uses are now a package export of `device-service-core` instead of a deep path into its test tree. ([#13457](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13457)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: a delivery id that the same device repeats after its 30-day receipt expired, while its row is still in the store, is answered from that row as deduplicated instead of failing with a raw unique-constraint error (the review of #13208). ([#13212](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13212)) ([#13279](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13279)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: a session whose file header cannot be read, or names a session kind this build does not know, is never started or reopened unattended. It is refused like a child or worker session instead of being treated as an ordinary interactive one (#13037). ([#13279](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13279)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- When another device refuses to wake a session there that is not running, the reason its delivery consumer gives is shown only when it is a short machine code; any other reason is shown as `unrecognised`. ([#13277](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13277), part of [#13037](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/13037)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))

### Added

- `omo remote bootstrap` and `omo remote enable` install and start one fixed, always-on per-user unit beside the OmO device service that runs the omo session host: the systemd user unit `omo-session-host.service` on Linux (enabled, restarted after every exit) and the LaunchAgent `ai.omo.session-host` on macOS (run at load, kept alive). It runs `omo daemon run --pinned` for the registered agent dir, and the device service's `OMO_RELAYD_SERVICES` table names it (entry `"omo"`) as the only unit it may start for a cold wake. The table keeps its other entries, and the device service restarts only when the table changed. `omo remote disable` disables and removes both, and while remote sessions are off a bootstrap removes them instead of installing them (#13594). ([#13595](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13595)) ([#13606](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13606))
- `omo daemon run --pinned` starts the operator host with no idle exit; a task host started from one of its sessions still idles out as usual (#13594). ([#13595](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13595)) ([#13606](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13606))
- Device service client: the delivery-consumer requests of #13037 (`deliveries.serve`, `delivery.answer`, `delivery.held`, `delivery.pending`, `delivery.drained`, `peer.admitted`) and their events (`delivery.inbound`, `delivery.holds`, `delivery.wake`), in the shapes omo-relay-daemon #1076 ships, behind `connectDeliveryConsumer` in `device-service-core`. The conformance fixtures are copied in-tree from that release. ([#13457](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13457)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: the engine's delivery consumer now connects to the device service through that client, so a delivery from another device for a session here that is not running is taken in, answered, and the session started. ([#13457](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13457)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: the session wake now loads from its own sidecar, `extensions/omo-wake.js` behind `#omo-wake-runtime`: the carrier and its host connection, the delivery consumer and the device-service client never enter the main `omo.js` bundle, which carries only three lazy shells (the session-start start, a send's same-device wake, the control endpoint's admission ask); a sidecar that fails to load answers as if no wake exists. Measured 1,547,852 -> 1,476,860 bytes on this branch; the byte ceiling in `bundle-budget.json` moves to 1,478,000 for it. ([#13455](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13455)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: the session wake of #13037 now runs in production, but only on an engine at or above the wake engine minimum `MIN_WAKE_ENGINE_VERSION` (A8.1): the first engine release that drops a woken session's retained record (senpi#6449). Below it no carrier starts, and a `thread_send` naming a session that is not running answers as it did before the wake existed (`queued_offline` with `reason: "wake_unavailable"`). At or above it, every `tui` or `rpc` engine (never a task child, never under CI) starts one carrier per agent directory on its first session start: it opens the session by path on the operator host that `thread_create` opens on, sends the engine's `wake`, and hands it back quietly once it has finished; the answer is then `queued` with `waiting_on: { kind: "wake" }`. It still follows `session_wake.same_device`, read for the target session's own project, which stays off by default. ([#13455](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13455)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: the carrier sweeps its woken rows on a timer only while the table holds a row (design A3.1.4: an empty table leaves no timer). ([#13455](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13455)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: a session's own inbox drain admits nothing while a carrier is opening it (A3.1.5). It asks the device service whether a row's sending device is admitted before it takes in a delivery from another device (5.6). ([#13455](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13455)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: the store can take in a delivery that another device's service attested for a session on this device that is not running (the intake row of #13037). The row is committed in the same transaction as a same-device delivery, keeps the sender's delivery id, text and display text, is rate-limited per sending device, and is admitted later under the engine's own ledger key, so the engine counts it once even if the same delivery also arrives live. A repeat of a delivery id from the same device is answered with the first answer. A reply to such a delivery continues its chain. ([#13208](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13208)) ([#13279](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13279)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: the store keeps a record of each session a wake asked for or opened (#13037): one row with its state, a lease and a generation that fences every write, at most 4 such sessions past `requested` per agent directory, and a transient open failure that returns the row to `requested` with its attempts and the time of the next one (the third deletes it). A wake primitive resolves a durable id to its one session file, refuses child and worker sessions, ensures the host and sends one plain `open_session` frame (no `attended`, no permission preset). ([#13212](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13212)) ([#13279](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13279)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: the pieces that will let a message from another of your signed-in devices reach a session that is not running on this device are the delivery consumer, the carrier that opens such a session in its own working directory and hands it back when its turn is done, and the pending sweep (#13037). ([#13220](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13220)) ([#13279](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13279)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- `omo remote wake [on|off|default]` reads or sets whether sessions on this device that are not running may be started by a message from your other signed-in devices; `default` follows the build's default, which is off. It needs device service 0.1.31 or later; on an older one the command sends nothing and says so. versions.body:
**Plain `omo login` signs a computer in from the terminal while OmO accounts are closed.** A computer with no OmO desktop app — a server over SSH, a fresh Linux box — runs `omo login`, gets a device code to approve on another device, and stores the credential in the OS credential store; the attach-before-mint refusal (#13096) answers a computer that already has its device before anything is asked of the service. The success line names the signed-in account (`Signed in to OmO as <email>.`), and `omo whoami` names it too; a failed account read still says how to see it. `omo logout` and `omo whoami` run while closed, so no message names a command that refuses. `login --help` describes the route (the command stays hidden from `omo --help`), every other closed `login` form refuses with a message that names the route, the closed hints name both routes, and the compiled entry classifies bare `login`, `logout` and `whoami` as one-shot launches with the same shared parse the command uses (`login --` included). The damaged-item message names the terminal route too instead of a desktop-app-only dead end. Tests run the flow through the npm launcher (against a service-auth bundle built from this source into a temp copy of the launcher tree), the compiled entry and the toolkit CLI, with an isolated HOME and runtime dir, no inherited session bus, an injected store, and a refusal-text assertion on every zero-mint case. ([#13281](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13281)) ([#13328](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13328))

**The computer-use conformance preflight tests pass on Windows.** The missing-driver message now prints its repo-relative path with forward slashes on every OS, so a run reads the same on every host, and the stdio-probe test builds its stand-in engine as a real executable for the host instead of a POSIX shell script. QA tooling only; no runtime behaviour changes. ([#13295](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13295), part of #13221)

**Computer use gets a declared-outcome conformance catalog for its QA.** `script/qa/computer/conformance/` adds a typed catalog in which every action, toolkit and mode cell on each OS declares that it delivers or refuses with an exact engine code, a report that fails a missing, duplicate, skipped or mis-coded cell or one that disturbed the person's session, an environment preflight that ends a broken host's run as `ENVIRONMENT_ERROR`, and twelve model-free reference tasks. QA tooling only; no runtime behaviour changes. ([#13241](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13241), part of #13221)

**The desktop session's actionability wait test no longer fails on a busy host.** The battery's wait now runs on an injectable clock: the host's monotonic time in a session, as before, and the fake backend's own clock in the test. So `the_battery_waits_for_an_element_that_appears_enabled_after_500_ms` checks the 500 ms wait in fake time instead of wall-clock bounds that host load could break. Runtime behaviour does not change. ([#13180](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13180), fixes #13178)

**A fuzzy handoff no longer fails on an account with many ended sessions, and never goes to a different session than an exact name would.** A fuzzy handoff first tries the thread's exact id, alias or name across every session, ended ones on other devices included, so a name that exactly matches one session always reaches that session. Otherwise local, live and ended sessions are compared together and the clearly best match wins wherever it lives; two equally good matches ask you to pick. Ended sessions that cannot match no longer count against the 500-candidate fuzzy cap, so a large history no longer blocks a unique match. ([#13141](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13141), follows #13066)

**A thread whose alias claim asks for a sign-in after it was created is still named by the alias.** When the account token expires between `thread_create` checking an alias and claiming it, the thread it already created is now named by the alias on its device and the call answers `ok` with `alias_scope: "local"`, instead of an error. `thread_rename` does the same when the account is gone by the claim. An alias used as a local name is now trimmed on every path. ([#13179](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13179), follows #13112) ([#13141](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13141))

**`omo login` no longer registers a second device for a computer that already has one.** Before any code, browser tab or new key, it checks the stored sign-in and the device the computer's OmO device service holds (parked included). A held, uncertain, locked or unreadable state refuses a new device and keeps the existing one, instead of adding an "omo CLI on <host>" row beside the desktop's. When the service advertises machine identity, both sign-in flows send a hashed hardware id (`SHA256("omo-machine-v1" + id)`; the raw id never leaves the computer), and a `machine_exists` refusal ends the sign-in without removing or taking over any device. ([#13096](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13096)) ([#13141](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13141))

**A thread alias no longer blocks thread creation when no account is signed in.** `thread_create` with an `alias` now creates the thread when the alias registry cannot get an account token. A desktop launch is always in that state. The alias becomes the thread's local name unless a `name` is given, and the result says the alias is local only (`alias_scope: "local"`). `thread_rename` with an alias does the same. Every other alias error is unchanged. ([#13112](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13112), fixes #13104)

Fixed: file reads through the bundled bunshin SDK over the relay work again (`readText`, `readBytes` and `read` no longer reject with "truncated must be a boolean for byte results"), an op sent with a minted capability token is no longer refused as malformed, and an unsupported `clientName` now fails at once with `invalid_client_name` naming the supported role. ([#13108](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13108))

**The machine-binding module no longer exports an unused helper.** `deviceProfileOf` from #13095 is now module-private, so the knip dead-code check on dev is green again. No behavior change. ([#13097](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13097))

**One computer is one OmO device: omo login binds to the machine's device service instead of registering its own.** A sign-in now advertises machine binding. When the service asks for the machine hash, omo asks this machine's device service (`device.machine_binding`) for it, and computes the same hash itself when no device service runs. The sign-in presents the device keys this machine already holds, so the service keeps the machine's existing device instead of adding a row.
